from inside CRMs, ticket close confirmation by AI call, workforce planning from outside systems and Workday, script forms, and a round of fixes.

Calling from inside CRMs: an agent can click a phone number in HubSpot, Salesforce, Dynamics 365, Zoho CRM or Freshdesk and the call dials on their open desk. Phone links elsewhere ask before dialling when the page is not listed, and the desk never dials a request by itself. Calls are logged against the CRM record that was clicked.

Ticket close confirmation: when a ticket is resolved, an AI call can ask the customer to confirm it is closed. The platform ends the call after the customer confirms, and the hold phrase can be set per agent. A resolved ticket can now be reopened for 2 days (was 7); a customer who writes in that time is asked whether it is about the ticket (YES reopens it, NEW opens a new ticket).

Workday and outside workforce planning: Workday can supply people, time off and paid hours, and an organisation can say that another system plans its schedules, with schedules coming in and stats and agent states going out, by connector (Puzzel) or by file feed. A later waiting file wins for the same agent and day. A new Integration sync area shows what was synced.

Calendar meetings and status: an available agent in a synced calendar meeting is set to In a calendar meeting and back afterwards. Per organisation, off by default.

Script forms: build forms with questions, branching pages, a shareable link and a responses report, beside the existing agent scripts.

Fixes: readiness no longer counts a standby partner's takeover set as down; the nightly backup reads the environment file safely and the update ensures the backup schedule; a login background picture of 1.4 MB no longer causes a server error; console sign-in shows the picture whole beside the form; the ? help button and buttons wear the brand's Main colour; the Academy practice organisation shows a Back to the Academy bar, also when the desk cannot sign in; and the Academy practice task for opening hours uses the screen's words."}
